first_impression.reaction: Fine. It says up front it isn't going to be a fluffy list: "Most lists of Macedonian wedding traditions stop at the party tricks." Then it hedges honestly in the key takeaways, which I prefer to being sold a 'rulebook'. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, it answered the basics plainly, so I went back and read the rest.

journey.quote: The parish priest sets the order of service, so ask your priest to walk you through it.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, and it doesn't pretend to know more than the church does. Good.

journey.quote: What follows is a guide to what you may see, not a rulebook.
journey.reaction: Honest about its limits. That's the kind of line that makes me trust the rest.

journey.quote: It is often told that the same kum will later be asked to baptise the couple's children, which is part of why the role is treated as a lifelong tie rather than a single day's job.
journey.reaction: "Often told" by who? It's fair to hedge, but the page says this kind of thing a lot (bread, water at the door, trousseau). After the third one it reads like nobody actually checked.

journey.quote: Wikipedia's account describes it as symbolising the farewell of villagers leaving home to work abroad.
journey.reaction: At least it's named, but Wikipedia is the source I'd check myself in ten seconds. Doesn't add authority.

journey.quote: Accounts differ on who can enter: one says couples from across North Macedonia compete to be chosen, while another says the couple has to originate from the village. Either way, it is a cultural event to watch, not a venue a visiting couple can book.
journey.reaction: This I like. It shows the conflict in the sources instead of picking one, and it tells me plainly I can't buy my way into it. No upsell.

journey.section: Marrying legally in North Macedonia as an Australian
journey.quote: This section is a starting point, not legal advice, and it reflects official sources as at November 2026.
journey.reaction: A date and a scope. Exactly what I want.

journey.quote: So the Certificate of No Impediment and any apostilles come from Belgrade, not Skopje.
journey.reaction: Concrete, useful, and the kind of detail a lazy blog gets wrong. I'd check it on the embassy site, but I expect it holds up.

journey.quote: Appointments are booked online, and the embassy states that fees apply for most services.
journey.reaction: Fees apply, but how much? Not a big deal, I can look it up, but a number or a link to the fee schedule would save me the trip.

journey.section: Marrying legally in North Macedonia as an Australian (CTA)
journey.quote: Your Advisor is a single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Better than most. A written fee is something. But it doesn't say whether you also take a cut from the venues and suppliers, which is the question I actually care about.

journey.quote: Whether you are keeping every custom your grandparents remember or choosing three that mean the most, the best weddings start with that family conversation.
journey.reaction: Bit of a greeting-card line to finish on. Harmless, but 'the best weddings' is the sort of thing I skip.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues and suppliers on top of the agreed fee?
What does the Advisor fee actually cover, and how is it calculated (flat, percentage, tiered)?
What do the Australian Embassy's notarial services (Certificate of No Impediment, apostille) actually cost, or where is the fee schedule?
Is a church wedding alone legally recognised in North Macedonia, or is a civil ceremony at the registry office required?
Where do the 'often told' customs come from: family accounts, ethnographic sources, or Wedded Wonderland's own weddings?
Has Wedded Wonderland actually planned a wedding in North Macedonia? A real example with the budget would tell me more than the CTA.

turn_offs_found.quote: the best weddings start with that family conversation.
turn_offs_found.why: An unsupported 'the best' line. Mild, but it's the emotional filler I tune out.

turn_offs_found.quote: Embroidered textiles and household linen are often told as the traditional heart of the trousseau, and some families pass pieces down through generations.
turn_offs_found.why: Repeated 'often told' attributions with no source make the cultural sections feel unchecked compared with the well-sourced legal section.

would_share_with: My partner, for the legal and dual-nationality section
Anyone in the family who wants to do part of it in North Macedonia

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like help with the paperwork, venues and travel, talk to a Wedded Advisor about a wedding in North Macedonia.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, so it doesn't annoy me, and 'fee agreed in writing' is a good start. I'd click through to look at the fee model, but I wouldn't enquire until I know whether you also earn from the suppliers.

top_3_changes: Next to the CTA, add one plain line (or a link) on whether Wedded Wonderland takes supplier commissions on top of the written fee. That's the deciding question for a reader like me.
Cut back the repeated 'often told' hedges or say where the account comes from, so the cultural sections match the sourcing standard of the legal section.
Link the Australian Embassy Belgrade fee schedule (or give a dated figure) where it says 'fees apply for most services'.
